formation.note: No fetched source states an explicit collaboration formation date. Wikipedia states data collection commenced 2018-04-01, but as a rank-12 source it may not be the sole source of a critical value, so no formation date is asserted.

intervals.label: collaboration
intervals.note: Start is conservatively taken from the confirmed 2023 relocation to Leibstadt rather than the unconfirmed ~2018 Brokdorf start (Wikipedia only); the collaboration in fact operated CONUS at Brokdorf earlier, but that start date is not sourced to a primary publication in this pass, so no earlier date is asserted (under-claiming per A17).
intervals.quote: In 2023, the Conus setup moved to another power plant in Leibstadt, Switzerland (KKL), since the reactor at KBR stopped operation

name: CONUS / CONUS+ Collaboration
notes: host_facility_id/host_site_id record the current (Leibstadt) location; the collaboration operated at facility:brokdorf-nuclear-power-plant from 2018-2023 (see experiment:conus facility_roles).

No official collaboration page with an institution/member count was found reachable in this pass; membership fields are left null per A17 rather than estimated from author lists on papers (explicitly forbidden by RESEARCH_AGENT_RULES rule 4/ontology ground rule).

The CONUS+ overview paper (arXiv:2407.11912) names the Max-Planck-Institut fur Kernphysik (MPIK) as the institution with the direct real-time network connection to the experiment, and other CONUS papers list co-authors from KIT, Duke University, PSI and the plant operators, but no single fetched source gives an authoritative institution count or list; formal institution rows are the membership-lead workstream's responsibility.
Derived field collaboration.experiment_ids is deliberately not written (v0.2 A1).

summary.plain: The physicists who built and run the CONUS and CONUS+ reactor-neutrino experiments, led from the Max Planck Institute for Nuclear Physics in Germany.
summary.technical: CONUS/CONUS+ collaboration, anchored at the Max-Planck-Institut fur Kernphysik (MPIK) Heidelberg with co-authors from institutions including KIT, Duke University and PSI on its publications; no official member/institution count located in this pass.
